---
title: "MRMhub-viz: Integration Visualizer"
description: |
  MRMhub-viz is a standalone, interactive tool for reviewing INTEGRATOR peak
  integration results and guiding the refinement of integration parameters.
---

**MRMhub-viz** is a standalone, interactive application for reviewing the peak-integration results
produced by INTEGRATOR (see [Running INTEGRATOR — Step 3](running.qmd)). It is distributed as a
self-contained executable (~10 MB), resides in the same folder as the **MRMhub** application, and is
launched like any other application. Because it reads the binary results written to the `misc/`
folder during peak integration, Step 3 must have been run at least once before the visualizer can
display a dataset.

## What it displays

The transition to be inspected is selected from the dropdown menu in the top-left corner. For the
selected transition, the extracted ion chromatograms of the individual samples are shown together
with the detected peak and its left and right integration borders, so that the integration can be
reviewed across the entire analytical sequence at a glance. Moving the pointer over a chromatogram
reports the exact retention time at the cursor — the value used when defining fixed peak borders in
the transition list (see [Input Files — Transition list](input-files.qmd)).

![](images/paste-12.png){fig-alt="Screenshot of the MRMhub-viz window for transition LPC 22:5 (570.4 to 184.1 m/z), selected from the dropdown at the top left. A grid of per-sample chromatogram panels, one per injection (labelled Longit_batch1_6, _7, _8 and so on), each plots intensity against retention time from about 1.6 to 2.6 minutes, with the detected peak and its left (blue) and right (orange) integration borders shaded."}

## The review → refine loop

MRMhub-viz is the inspection half of an iterative loop between visual review and parameter
adjustment. Automated integration is rarely optimal for every feature on the first pass; the
visualizer identifies where it fails, and the input files are adjusted to correct it. A typical
cycle proceeds as follows.

1. **Inspect.** Step through the transitions and confirm that the intended peak is detected and
   correctly bounded, both in the reference samples and across the sequence. Look for missed peaks,
   co-integrated neighbours, truncated tails, and failures of retention-time tracking.
2. **Diagnose.** Relate each problem to the setting responsible for it — a missed peak to `RT_tol`
   or `RT_shift`, a co-integrated neighbour to `peak_width`, an untracked retention-time jump to
   `RT_shift_bound` (see [Effects of the key settings](input-files.qmd#effects-of-the-key-settings)).
3. **Refine.** Adjust the global parameters in `param.txt`, or add per-feature overrides in the
   transition list (`peak width`, `uniform_width`, fixed integration bounds) for the problematic
   minority. Individual peaks that resist automated integration can also have their borders edited
   directly in `RT_matrix.csv`.
4. **Re-integrate.** After a change to `param.txt` or the transition list, re-run peak finding
   (Steps 1–2) followed by integration (Step 3); when only `RT_matrix.csv` has been edited, re-run
   Step 3 alone. Reload the dataset in MRMhub-viz and repeat until the integration is satisfactory.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Refine globally first, then per-feature.** Tune `param.txt` so that the majority of peaks
integrate correctly, and reserve transition-list overrides and fixed borders for the remaining
difficult peaks. Confirm every change in MRMhub-viz before re-integrating the whole dataset — see the
[peak-width recommendations](input-files.qmd#recommendations-for-setting-peak-integration-parameters).
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
**Re-running Step 2 overwrites `RT_matrix.csv`.** Any manual edits to the integration borders are
lost when peak finding is re-run. Make manual `RT_matrix.csv` adjustments only once the automated
integration is otherwise final, then run Step 3 (see [Running INTEGRATOR — Step 2](running.qmd)).
:::
